nuance: 시제 is not just past, present, and future labels. It is how the listener tracks whether an event happened, is happening, or is planned.
mistakes: Mixing past and present in one story without reason.
Forgetting that Korean future or intention can use -(으)ㄹ 거예요, -겠습니다, or -(으)려고 하다 depending on register and meaning.
Changing a sentence from casual to formal but leaving the tense or aspect inconsistent.

examples: 공식 이메일에서는 그래서보다 따라서가 더 자연스러울 수 있어요.
In a formal email, 따라서 may be more natural than 그래서.
Register affects connector choice.
반대 내용을 말할 때는 연결어를 그러나로 바꿔 보세요.
When saying opposing content, try changing the connector to 그러나.
Connector follows the relationship between ideas.
연결어 하나가 글의 논리를 완전히 바꿀 수 있어요.
One connector can completely change the logic of the writing.
Important synthesis point.
nuance: 연결어 is about logic, not decoration. A connector tells the reader how to understand the next sentence.
mistakes: Using 그래서 for every result even in formal writing.
Using 즉 when the next sentence adds new information instead of restating the same point.
Choosing connectors by English translation without checking the sentence relationship.

examples: 공식 이메일에서는 문체를 끝까지 격식 있게 맞춰야 해요.
In a formal email, the style should stay formal until the end.
Register consistency.
따라서와 ㅋㅋ가 한 문단에 같이 나오면 문체가 섞여 보여요.
If 따라서 and ㅋㅋ appear in the same paragraph, the style looks mixed.
Connects chapters 63 and 64.
카톡 답장과 면접 답변은 문체부터 달라야 해요.
A KakaoTalk reply and an interview answer need to differ from the style level onward.
Final synthesis of register choice.
nuance: 문체 is broader than one polite ending. It covers the whole feel of the text: vocabulary, endings, connectors, and sentence shape.
mistakes: Adding -요 to casual slang and assuming the 문체 is now polite.
Using formal connectors while keeping casual endings in the same paragraph.
Changing vocabulary but forgetting to change sentence endings and connectors.

usage: The vehicle you board takes 을/를.
examples: 시간이 없으면 택시로 가세요.
If you do not have time, go by taxi.
택시로 marks the means of travel.
비가 와서 택시를 탔어요.
It rained, so I took a taxi.
택시를 타다 is the boarding/taking frame.
택시 좀 불러 주세요.
Please call me a taxi.
A practical request at hotels, restaurants, and stations.
nuance: 택시로 가요 and 택시를 타요 are both natural, but they answer different questions: method versus boarding action.
mistakes: Saying 택시에 가요 for 'by taxi.' Use 택시로 가요.
Forgetting 을/를 in 택시를 타요 when the focus is taking the vehicle.
Using 택시로 타요; 타다 takes the vehicle as object, not method.

usage: to get off at the stop
The place where the action happens takes 에서.
examples: 버스 타러 정류장에 가요.
I go to the bus stop to take the bus.
타러 gives purpose; 정류장에 gives destination.
다음 정류장에서 내려요.
Get off at the next stop.
내리다 happens at the stop, so 에서.
버스 정류장이 어디예요?
Where is the bus stop?
Useful direction question.
nuance: 정류장 is the stop itself. 역 is a station, usually larger and often for subway or train.
mistakes: Using 역 for every bus stop. For buses, 정류장 is normally better.
Saying 정류장으로 내려요. Use 정류장에서 내려요 because getting off happens at the stop.
Forgetting the destination/action split: 정류장에 가요, 정류장에서 기다려요.

examples: 시청역에서 환승해요.
I transfer at City Hall Station.
The station where transferring happens takes 에서.
2호선으로 갈아타야 해요.
You have to transfer to Line 2.
The line you transfer into takes 으로.
환승하려면 어디로 가요?
Where do I go to transfer?
A practical station question.
nuance: 환승 is the noun and official transit word; 갈아타다 is the everyday action verb.
mistakes: Using 환승 as if it were only a subway word. It can apply to buses and transport modes too.
Saying 2호선에 갈아타요. In route instructions, 2호선으로 갈아타요 is clearer.
Forgetting that the transfer location takes 에서: 시청역에서 환승해요.

usage: to receive medicine at the pharmacy
examples: 처방전을 가지고 약국에 가요.
I take the prescription to the pharmacy.
Clinic-to-pharmacy flow.
약국에서 약 먹는 시간을 확인했어요.
I checked the medicine schedule at the pharmacy.
Pharmacy context for instructions.
약국이 병원 옆에 있어요.
The pharmacy is next to the clinic.
Existence location uses 에.
nuance: 약국 is where medicine is dispensed or sold. 병원 is where you see the doctor; 약국 is where you usually receive the medicine afterward.
mistakes: Using 병원 for the pharmacy step. After receiving a prescription, you usually go to 약국.
Saying 약국에서 가요 for destination. Use 약국에 가요.
Forgetting that the pharmacist is 약사, not 의사.

examples: 병원에서 처방전을 받았어요.
I got a prescription at the clinic.
The clinic is the action place, so 에서.
처방전을 약국에 내야 해요.
You have to hand in the prescription at the pharmacy.
Instruction with -아/어야 해요.
처방전 없이 살 수 있는 약도 있어요.
There are also medicines you can buy without a prescription.
Useful pharmacy distinction.
nuance: 처방전 is not the medicine itself. It is the document or order that lets the pharmacy prepare the medicine.
mistakes: Confusing 처방전 with 약. 약 is medicine; 처방전 is the prescription.
Using 처방전 for general advice. It specifically refers to a prescription.
Forgetting the clinic-pharmacy sequence: 병원에서 처방전을 받고 약국에서 약을 받다.

examples: 이 원룸은 보증금이 얼마예요?
How much is the deposit for this studio?
The deposit is the first cost to ask about.
보증금은 500만 원이고 월세는 70만 원이에요.
The deposit is 5 million won and the monthly rent is 700,000 won.
보증금 and 월세 are a pair in listings.
계약서에서 보증금 반환 조건을 확인해 두세요.
Check the deposit return conditions in the contract in advance.
Practical contract review sentence.
nuance: 보증금 is not rent. It is a deposit paid upfront and normally returned after the lease, depending on the contract and room condition.
mistakes: Asking only 월세 and forgetting 보증금. Korean housing cost is usually a pair.
Confusing 보증금 with 계약금. 계약금 is a contract/down payment; 보증금 is the housing deposit.
Forgetting to check return conditions before signing.

usage: How much is the monthly rent?
examples: 월세는 70만 원이에요.
The monthly rent is 700,000 won.
Listing cost sentence.
관리비가 따로면 실제 월세가 더 비싸게 느껴져요.
If the maintenance fee is separate, the actual monthly rent feels more expensive.
Real monthly cost depends on separate fees.
전세보다 월세 원룸을 찾고 있어요.
I am looking for a monthly-rent studio rather than jeonse.
Lease type contrast.
nuance: 월세 is the monthly rent payment. 관리비 and utilities may or may not be included, so ask 따로예요? and 포함돼 있어요?
mistakes: Treating 월세 as the full monthly cost without checking 관리비.
Confusing 월세 with 전세. 전세 uses a large deposit instead of ordinary monthly rent.
Forgetting the object phrase in 월세를 내다.

examples: 미세먼지가 심하면 일정은 취소하는 게 좋겠어요.
If the fine dust is bad, it would be better to cancel the plan.
Weather condition leading to a decision.
미세먼지 때문에 산책을 못 했어요.
I could not take a walk because of the fine dust.
N 때문에 with a weather/air-quality noun.
오늘 미세먼지 수치를 확인하고 나가세요.
Check today's fine dust level before going out.
Practical Korean daily-life warning.
nuance: 미세먼지 is not ordinary dust in your room. It refers to air pollution particles reported in forecasts and apps.
mistakes: Translating it as simple 먼지 when the topic is air quality. Use 미세먼지.
Forgetting that 미세먼지 often changes outdoor plans in Korea.
Using 좋다/나쁘다 without context; 미세먼지가 심하다 is the clearest beginner phrase.

usage: to top up a transit card
The card is the object being topped up.
Please top it up with 10,000 won.
Natural request at a station or convenience store.
충전 often comes with checking the remaining balance.
examples: 교통카드에 만 원 충전해 주세요.
Please top up my transit card with 10,000 won.
에 marks where the money is added.
지하철 타기 전에 교통카드를 충전했어요.
I topped up my transit card before taking the subway.
A practical pre-ride action.
잔액이 부족하면 여기서 충전하세요.
If the balance is low, top it up here.
Connects the balance problem to the action.
nuance: For transit cards, 충전 is a top-up. For phones, it is battery charging. The object matters: 교통카드를 충전하다 versus 휴대폰을 충전하다.
mistakes: Using 사다 for adding money to a transit card. Buy the card with 사다, but add value with 충전하다.
Saying 돈을 교통카드에서 충전해요. Use 교통카드에 충전해요 because the money is added onto the card.
Confusing 충전 with 잔액. 충전 is the action; 잔액 is the remaining balance.

usage: The ticket object in train travel.
예매하다 is the advance booking action.
매진 describes ticket or seat availability.
examples: 부산 가는 KTX 표를 예매하려고 해요.
I am trying to book a KTX ticket to Busan.
The chapter's core ticket-counter sentence.
부산 가는 표 있어요?
Are there tickets to Busan?
Natural availability question.
표가 매진이면 다음 기차를 확인하세요.
If the tickets are sold out, check the next train.
Ticket availability plus fallback.
nuance: 표 is the general ticket word. 입장권 is more specifically an admission ticket for entering a venue, so KTX 표 should not be replaced with 입장권.
mistakes: Using 입장권 for KTX tickets. For trains, 표 is the natural general word.
Confusing 표 with 매표소. 표 is the ticket; 매표소 is the place that sells tickets.
Forgetting the counter 장 when buying: 표 한 장 주세요.

english: final consonant at the bottom of a syllable block
examples: 한에는 받침 ㄴ이 있어요.
한 has the final consonant ㄴ.
한 = ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ.
nuance: 받침 is a role inside a block, not just the name of a consonant. The same ㄴ can be an initial consonant or a 받침 depending on position.
mistakes: Do not put a space between the block and 에는: 한에는, not 한 에는.
